key_insight: Generalized Residual Closure (GRC) frames continual learning as recursively closing future-relevant residuals, so a model can learn new tasks while preserving prior responsibilities and the ability to learn again.
engineering_relevance: For constitutive modeling and other safety-critical AI systems, GRC provides a principled update rule that balances stability, plasticity, and future-safe reuse of learned behavior.
method: Defines two primitive learning modes: transformation within a representation and revision of the representation itself.
Derives a local tangent decomposition and a criterion for when representation revision is required.
In an affine setting, proves a necessary-and-sufficient compatibility condition and a unique constrained quadratic update that preserves registered legacy responsibilities while reducing residuals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations and proof-based results, including compatibility conditions, uniqueness of the update, and operator comparisons, rather than experimental dataset evaluation.
watch_item: The framework relies on regularity assumptions and an abstract learner-world boundary, so practical implementation may be sensitive to model specification and how ‘registered responsibilities’ are defined.
paper_title: Generalized Residual Closure: General Learning Dynamics for Stability-Plasticity Compatibility
